info.title: GMD API v2.0
info.description:
Gracenote Music API Specification
GMD API V2.0

get.description: Text search for `Artist` objects using artist name.

Get `Artist` object(s) by ID

**Notes** * Objects are returned in order requested. * If an object is not found, a `null` value is returned in its position. * Duplicate ids in the query will result in duplicate objects in the response * TMS Party ID lookups require TMS ID add-on. * Spotify Artist ID lookups require Spotify IDs add-on.

**Example:** Lookup by Gracenote ID
`https://.../artists/gnid?ids=GND6CJFDB6BH1X3`

**Example:** Lookup by tms-music-party-id
`https://.../artists/tms-music-party-id?ids=521029`

**Example:** Lookup by spotify-artist-id
`https://.../artists/spotify-artist-id?ids=0d25ed8c5cc94cdbaf8e9961419ed6be`

Text search for `Recording` objects using recording name and/or artist name.

Note that one of either recording or artist name is required. Omitting both will result in an error.

Get `Recording` object(s) by ID

**Notes** * Objects are returned in order requested. * If an object is not found, a `null` value is returned in its position. * Duplicate ids in the query will result in duplicate objects in the response

**Example:** Lookup by Gracenote ID
`https://.../recordings/gnid?ids=GN0TR5Z86C868HS`

**Example:** Lookup by ISRC
`https://.../recordings/isrc?ids=DEY371001140`

Text search for `Album` objects using album name and/or artist name.

Note that one of either album or artist name is required. Omitting both will result in an error.

Get `Album` object(s) by ID

**Notes** * Objects are returned in order requested. * If an object is not found, a `null` value is returned in its position. * Duplicate ids in the query will result in duplicate objects in the response

**Example:** Lookup by Gracenote ID
`https://.../albumEditions/gnid?ids=GN949Y7H6M9XNYP`

The descriptor correlation API enables the computation of Artist and Recording similarity by providing numerical values representing that similarity. These similarity values can be used to inform music discovery and catalog navigation models and algorithms.

The following workflow illustrates how correlates are used to show that the genre **Psychedelic Rock** is more similar to **Post-Modern Rock** than it is to **Ragtime**.

1. The `/descriptors/genre` API is used to determine that the `genreID` for "Psychedelic Rock" is `2844`.
``` curl https:///descriptors/genre ... { { "ID": "2844", "genericName": "Psychedelic Rock" } ... }, ```

2. The `/descriptors/descriptorCorrelations` API is used with `genreID` value `2844` and the descriptor type set to "genres".
``` curl https:///descriptorCorrelations/genres?ids=2844 ... { { "ID": "33121", "genre": "Post-Modern Rock", "weight": "200" }, { "ID": "3128", "genre": "Ragtime", "weight": "-700" } ... } ```

3. The results show that **Post-Modern Rock** is correlated to **Psychedelic Rock** with a weight of **200** while **Ragtime** is correlated with weight of **-700**. Therefore, **Post-Modern Rock** is the most similar genre.
